clue.text: Not like a hypocrite from the time of joining bank

parts.note: since means from the time of, as in 'since Monday'
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: Someone has been honest ever since they started working at a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a noun for a financial firm, but it is the verb, as in 'bank on'; 'joining' simply links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypocrite feigns feelings, so someone acting genuinely and without pretence behaves the opposite way.

clue.text: Lined up, having a quarrel

explanation.surface: Soldiers stood in line while bickering among themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means placed one after another in a line, and also, with 'row' as a British word for argument, engaged in a dispute.

clue.text: Ape jumps over an awning

indicators.note: the word for ape leaps across the little word an, so it ends up on both sides of it

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey leaps over a shop's sunshade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ape' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning imitate; 'jumps over' straddles AN, giving C-AN-OPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are overhead coverings of fabric giving shelter, so an awning is a kind of canopy.

clue.text: Engineers getting wrong sort of answer

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Army engineers are given the wrong kind of reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' looks like an adjective qualifying 'sort', but it is a noun: a TORT is a civil wrong in law. 'getting' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a sharp or witty reply, one particular kind of response.

clue.text: Requirements for baby nevertheless coming in after time

indicators.note: the word for nevertheless enters the word for after time and sits inside it

parts.note: late means after the expected time
yet means nevertheless, as in 'and yet'

explanation.surface: Baby supplies, it turns out, have nevertheless arrived late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after time' is one idea: arriving after the expected time is being LATE. 'coming in' puts the word for nevertheless inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the full set of clothes and bedding bought for a newborn.

clue.text: A jolly fuss about sick animal

parts.note: taken as written
a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

indicators.note: the word for fuss goes round the word for sick, holding it inside

parts.note: ado is fuss, as in 'much ado'
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone makes a cheerful fuss over an ailing pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like an adjective, but in crosswords a Jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine. 'about' wraps the fuss round the sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: A comedian could come from this country

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase can be rearranged to form the country named, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a certain comic might hail from this nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could come from this' tells you to rearrange the letters of A COMEDIAN to make the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia, now North Macedonia, is a Balkan nation; the name also covers a wider historic region.

clue.text: Padre does reform a criminal

indicators.note: to reform is to re-form, reshaping the letters of the two words beside it

explanation.surface: A priest succeeds in turning a lawbreaker into a better person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' looks like the priest's moral work, but it is the signal to rearrange PADRE DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, a bandit of the Wild West kind.

clue.text: Produce a box with right content

annotationWithheld.why: 'Produce a box with right content' (6) for CREATE: CRATE (box) needs an E inside it, and no clue word gives E ('right' is R or RT); the clue looks garbled and no source online gives another wording
annotationWithheld.clue: Produce a box with right content

clue.text: Mum at home stops people being big supporters

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
in means at home, as in 'staying in'
to stay someone is to halt or check them

explanation.surface: A mother stays in, keeping people from becoming big fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' looks like the verb of the sentence, but with 'people' it gives STAYS, in the sense of halting someone; 'being' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the chief support of something, originally the stay holding a ship's mainmast.

clue.text: Invent lipstick say?

explanation.surface: A question of whether lipstick counts as dreaming something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To concoct a story is to fabricate it; cosmetics such as lipstick are collectively called by the same two-word noun.

clue.text: Like certain hospitality? Gosh - - endless meat consumed!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

indicators.note: the word for meat loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: pork is a meat
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: At a business entertainment, someone exclaims that all the meat has been eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims the last letter from PORK, leaving POR. Corporate hospitality is a company entertaining clients, often at sporting events.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporate hospitality means a business treating clients, so the adjective describing that entertaining relates to companies.

clue.text: Liveliness and energy coming to old city after six

indicators.note: after sends the energy and old city pieces to follow the number, though the clue names them first

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
go means energy or drive, as in 'full of go'
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone gains new energy after visiting an ancient city at six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names energy and the old city first, but 'after six' puts them behind the numeral. 'and' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour is physical or mental strength and energy, a synonym for vitality.

clue.text: Worrying sign group's given

parts.note: a badge is an emblem or sign
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A group has been handed a troubling omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'group's given' reads as 'group has been given', so the group follows the sign; 'Worrying' means pestering, not anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgering is pestering someone persistently, a synonym for harassing or nagging.

clue.text: Asians win a seat after struggling against English

indicators.note: the three words are shaken up, as if struggling, before the final letter is added

explanation.surface: An Asian party fights to win a parliamentary seat against the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after struggling' rearranges WIN A SEAT; 'against' sets E beside it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Taiwanese people are inhabitants of Taiwan, an island nation in East Asia.

clue.text: Groomed fellow all the better for my treatment

parts.note: man means fellow

parts.words: all the better for my treatment
parts.note: a patient who recovers after my care can be described with 'I cured'

explanation.surface: A man looks much better after the speaker has looked after him.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece is a whimsical paraphrase: someone 'all the better for my treatment' is someone I CURED.
explanation.definitionFit: Manicured means neatly trimmed and tidy, like hands or a lawn given careful attention.

clue.text: Crook with no name in plot

indicators.note: the word for crook is left without the letter for name, so that letter drops out

parts.note: a crook is a bend, as in the crook of an arm

explanation.surface: A villain who is anonymous figures in a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal, and 'plot' a conspiracy; in fact the crook is a BEND and the plot is a garden bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of ground for growing flowers or vegetables is a garden bed.

clue.text: Exclusion makes group finish prematurely

indicators.note: the word for group stops one letter short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a band is a group, of musicians for example

explanation.surface: A musical group gets barred and has to end its set early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finish prematurely' cuts the last letter from BAND; 'makes' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ban is a prohibition, which excludes someone or something.

clue.text: Being teetotal could be boring

explanation.surface: Abstaining from alcohol might make someone dull company.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstaining from alcohol is said to have gone without drink; a lecture lacking interest is likewise flat and dull.

clue.text: State gets scientific institute to take on a graduate

annotationWithheld.why: 'State gets scientific institute to take on a graduate' (7) for ALABAMA: A+LAB+A+MA needs two As but the clue has only one 'a', and no other word supplies the first A; no source online gives another wording
annotationWithheld.clue: State gets scientific institute to take on a graduate

clue.text: Dallier, having switched sides, got better

indicators.note: the word's two sides, its first and last letters, change places, rearranging the word

explanation.surface: A time-waster changed allegiance and recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having switched sides' swaps the first and last letters of DALLIER, D and R. 'switched sides' looks political, like a defector, but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who rallied recovered strength after illness, a synonym for improved.

clue.text: No horse's sound can be heard

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so its sound gives a word spelt differently

parts.note: the noise a horse makes is a neigh

explanation.surface: A horse's whinny is audible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be heard' signals a word said aloud: NEIGH, spoken, gives a word spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old-fashioned or parliamentary word for a negative vote or reply.

clue.text: Neighbour providing a dairy product

parts.note: butter is a product made from milk

explanation.surface: The person next door supplies something from the dairy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'providing' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An abutter is someone whose land borders another's, chiefly a legal term for an adjoining owner.

clue.text: Knight, a funny fellow returning home

indicators.note: the phrase before it is read in the opposite direction, coming back on itself

parts.note: taken as written
a wag is a joker or wit
in means at home

explanation.surface: A comic knight comes back to his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns A WAG to give GAWA, which is followed by IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain is one of King Arthur's Round Table knights, hero of the Green Knight legend.

clue.text: Miner who gave a hand to secretaries?

definitions.text: who gave a hand to secretaries?

explanation.surface: A coal miner who helped out office staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hand' is a style of writing: Isaac Pitman devised the shorthand system long used by secretaries.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitman works in a coal pit; Sir Isaac Pitman invented a widely taught system of shorthand writing.

clue.text: A time with clucking females in foreign city

parts.note: taken as written
hens are female birds that cluck

explanation.surface: A spell spent among clucking poultry in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'in' are link words joining the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital of Greece, a city abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Ascetic type sitting in wilderness, enervated

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters spanning the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A hermit sitting in the desert, drained of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sitting in' points to letters inside WILDERNESS ENERVATED.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ancient Jewish sect living austere communal lives, some in the Judean desert.

clue.text: Isn't participating in search? That's most odd

indicators.note: the word for isn't takes part inside the word for search, sitting within it

parts.note: a quest is a search
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone declines to join a hunt, and that's very peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'participating in' sets the colloquial form of isn't inside the search; 'That's' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaint means oddly old-fashioned or unusual, so the superlative is the most peculiar.

clue.text: Come to an end being dismissed as a cricketer

explanation.surface: A batsman's innings finishes when he is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman is run out when fielders break the wicket before he completes a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies that are exhausted have been used up; a batsman caught short of the crease is given out that way.

clue.text: What's troubled me — dad's pet bolted

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed and jumbled, as something troubled is

explanation.surface: Someone asks what has upset them: the family pet has run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges ME DAD'S PET, where the apostrophe S counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To stampede is to rush off in panic, as a frightened herd does, a synonym for fled.

clue.text: Had a bite in new hut (egg eaten)

indicators.note: the letter for egg is swallowed up inside the letters for new and hut

parts.note: a shed is a hut
O looks like an egg, a crossword convention

explanation.surface: Someone snacked in a newly built hut, where an egg was eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten' puts O inside N + SHED. 'nosh' is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: To nosh is informal British slang for eating, so having a snack is noshing.

clue.text: One playing tricks awfully pert — offensive son kept in

indicators.note: the word for offensive and the letter for son are held inside the rearranged letters
the letters are treated badly and scrambled

parts.note: rank means offensive, as of a smell

explanation.surface: An impertinent joker is kept in after school for being offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles PERT to PTER; 'kept in' then holds the offensive word and son inside those four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster is a practical joker, someone who plays pranks on others.
